_comment: Tuning set for M5 crux detection. Supplied by Noah, including the expected crux for each debate — that column is the answer key. The measure of success is not whether the model outputs something plausible, but whether its crux matches expectedCrux in substance.

debates.topic: AI will create more jobs than it destroys
debates.sideA: New technologies have always created new industries and employment. AI will raise productivity and generate new kinds of work.
debates.sideB: This wave is different because AI automates cognitive work itself, potentially eliminating many jobs faster than new ones appear.
debates.expectedCrux: Whether AI-driven productivity creates enough new demand and occupations to offset automation, and over what time horizon.

debates.sideA: Everyone should receive an unconditional income to reduce poverty and prepare for automation.
debates.sideB: Guaranteed income weakens work incentives and is an inefficient use of public money.
debates.expectedCrux: Empirical disagreement about how people respond to unconditional cash and whether the benefits outweigh the costs.

debates.sideA: Nuclear energy is one of the safest low-carbon electricity sources and is necessary for decarbonization.
debates.sideB: It is too expensive, too slow to build, and poses waste and accident risks.
debates.expectedCrux: Whether cost and deployment speed matter more than nuclear's reliability and low emissions.

debates.sideA: Most knowledge work can be done just as effectively from home, with happier employees.
debates.sideB: In-person work improves collaboration, mentoring, creativity, and organizational culture.
debates.expectedCrux: How much informal interaction contributes to long-term productivity compared with flexibility and autonomy.

debates.sideA: Platforms should moderate harmful misinformation and abusive content.
debates.sideB: Heavy moderation risks censorship and suppresses legitimate debate.
debates.expectedCrux: Where to draw the line between reducing harm and protecting free expression.

debates.sideA: A degree still substantially increases lifetime earnings and opportunities.
debates.sideB: Tuition has risen so much that many degrees no longer justify their cost.
debates.expectedCrux: Whether the average return on higher education remains positive after accounting for debt, field of study, and alternatives.

debates.sideA: Open models promote innovation, transparency, and broad access.
debates.sideB: Restricting advanced models reduces misuse and allows safer deployment.
debates.expectedCrux: Whether openness produces greater net benefits or greater net risks.

debates.sideA: Higher minimum wages improve living standards with little effect on employment.
debates.sideB: Higher wage floors reduce hiring, especially for low-skill workers.
debates.expectedCrux: The size of the employment effects relative to the gains for workers who remain employed.
